intended_application: biofilm to control post-harvest fungal decay of organically grown apples during storage

process_steps.description: Sodium alginate solution heated with constant agitation until fully dissolved

source.quote: the coating solution (2% sodium alginate) was heated at 70 °C with constant agitation until all of the powder was completely dissolved

process_steps.description: Glycerol added and stirred at room temperature

source.quote: glycerol was added to the solution and the mixture was left to stir for 1 h at room temperature

process_steps.description: Yeast cultivated in YPD liquid medium overnight

source.quote: Yeasts were cultivated in YPD liquid medium overnight

process_steps.description: Cells harvested by centrifugation at 2500 × g and washed with sterile water

source.quote: cells were harvested by centrifugation at 2500× g for 20 min and washed with sterile water

process_steps.description: Yeast cell suspension added to the alginate solution and stirred

source.quote: the killer strain was incorporated by adding the suspension of yeast cells into the alginate coating solution and the mixture was stirred for 10 min

process_steps.description: 20 mL poured onto 90 mm Petri dishes

source.quote: The film-forming solutions (20 mL) were poured onto Petri dishes (90 mm diameter)

recipes.description: Sodium alginate film with glycerol and Wickerhamomyces anomalus CBS 1982 killer yeast cells

source.quote: sodium alginate (CAS No 9005-38-3, Sigma Aldrich: Steinheim, Germany; 2% w/v)

ingredients.name: Wickerhamomyces anomalus CBS 1982 killer yeast cells

source.quote: The concentration of the killer yeast cells was fixed to have a final concentration of ~6 logs CFU/cm2 in the bioactive film

properties.name: tensile_strength
properties.test_details: 20 mm × 100 mm strips, 50 mm grip separation, 60 mm/min

properties.name: elongation_at_break
properties.test_details: 20 mm × 100 mm strips, 50 mm grip separation, 60 mm/min

properties.name: other
properties.name_reported: W. anomalus survival in the film
properties.test_details: after 28 days at 2 °C then 14 days at 22 °C

source.quote: The population of W. anomalus immobilized in the alginate film at the end of the storage remained above 75%

properties.name: antimicrobial_activity
properties.name_reported: P. italicum decay incidence on coated apples
properties.test_details: wounded apples inoculated with P. italicum, dip-coated, 28 days at 2 °C then 14 days at 22 °C; uncoated control about 90%

source.quote: the decay incidence of fruits coated with alginate biofilms containing W. anomalus or P. membranifaciens was about 35% and 75%, respectively

gaps: solvent for the 2% sodium alginate solution (not named)
yeast cell concentration added to the solution (only the target ~6 log CFU/cm2 in the dried film is given)

best_recipes.criterion: limiting post-harvest fungal decay of apples

source.quote: Alginate biofilms containing W. anomalus killer yeasts could be effective in limiting post-harvest fungal decay losses in organically grown apples
